lines.text: Every checkout has one card field. A group is never one person. So one person fronts it all, then chases everyone back.
Sutra splits the purchase before anyone pays.
Eighteen thousand six hundred rupees, two people.
Each gets their own permission, capped at exactly their share, on their own card.
Everyone approves, or nobody is charged.
This isn't a mockup.
Here is the live receipt: both people charged, nine thousand three hundred each, through Prava's real sandbox, a real card network, test money.
The receipt is hash-chained and signed, and anyone can verify it offline against the engine's public key.
Around the mechanism, a full product.
A dashboard that shows exactly what your card is exposed to, usually nothing.
A store shelf where card-rail products are marked.
And a builder that shows every cap before anyone commits.
Planning starts as a sentence: dinner Saturday, near Koramangala, under nine hundred each.
Each person answers privately.
The board ranks real OpenStreetMap venues, and every score explains itself.
Arithmetic, not a guess, and answering never authorises a rupee.
Paste a restaurant bill and Sutra reconciles it against the printed total, then splits by who claimed what, and charges nothing, honestly zero.
Tag the bot in the thread: it answers from the group's real state, and refuses anything payment-shaped.
The same protocol ships as a NANDA Town plugin, an open pull request upstream.
Four agents run a group purchase; one declines, and a backstop absorbs the shortfall.
NANDA's own prepaid plugin can't do this, it pools one balance.
Sutra caps each agent on its own mandate.
No pooled wallet. Nobody fronting anyone else. Either everyone is charged, one after another, each with its own retry, or nobody is. Split it before you pay it.
